newsitem.title: USA: Dow is denied delay in implant suit trial.
newsitem.headline: Dow is denied delay in implant suit trial.

text.p: A federal judge in Michigan denied a motion from Dow Chemical Co and Dow Corning Corp to suspend an earlier ruling allowing a Louisiana trial of a breast implant suit to continue, the court said Tuesday.
The companies had asked U.S. District Judge Denise Page Hood to stay her earlier ruling until the firms could ask the U.S. Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals to review it.
Hood ruled last week that the first two phases of a nine-week-old trial of a class action suit against Dow Chemical in Louisiana Civil District Court in New Orleans can proceed.

The Louisiana trial re-started May 22. The trial had been halted by a May 8 ruling from the appeals court that all state and federal breast implant cases against Dow Chemical and Corning Inc be consolidated in federal court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

Dow Chemical and Corning each own 50 percent of Dow Corning. Women suing the companies allege silicone gel breast implants made by Dow Corning have caused atypical connective tissue health problems. The companies deny the allegations.

Hood's latest ruling came May 23 but was not released by the court until today. In denying the motion, Hood sided with plaintiffs, who argue that the public interest for a timely resolution of the case would be harmed if a stay were granted.
"The plaintiffs are currently in trial and their right to a jury trial should not be further delayed," Hood wrote.
Dow spokesmen could not be reached for comment.
